sub.name: Continuity and responsiveness
sub.example: T5 presses T4's gap; T6 answers T5's wind claim directly.
sub.limitation: minor: T8 opens geography thread loosely tied to T7's forecast point.

sub.name: Development of ideas
sub.example: T6 introduces warehouse vs delivery-truck distinction; T7 builds forecasts on it.
sub.limitation: minor: T10 fragility-vs-contribution distinction arrives last, never used.

sub.name: Exploration of central tensions
sub.example: Ocean versus winds credit split examined across T4-T7.
sub.limitation: minor: nobody raises cold northerly flow over eastern Canada from Rockies-shaped wind patterns.

sub.name: Integration of perspectives
sub.example: T9 Tracer narrows to 'one major link in a chain' after T8.
sub.limitation: minor: Ice-Core Reader's paleo evidence barely reshapes Comparer's position.

sub.name: Progress toward understanding
sub.example: T10 sharpens open question: fragile link versus largest contributor.
sub.limitation: minor: actual ocean-atmosphere split never estimated, left wholly open.

criteria.name: Quality of disagreement, trust and grounding

sub.name: Faithful engagement
sub.example: T5 restates T4's switched-off-current test accurately before objecting.
sub.limitation: minor: T2 calls Gulf Stream 'supporting actor' without engaging T1's magnitude claim.

sub.name: Substance of challenges
sub.example: T5: current shutoff measures added heat, not whether winds do most work; T6 answers.
sub.limitation: minor: T3's 'size of the gap' rebuttal asserted without any figures.

sub.name: Accuracy and support
sub.example: Labrador Current, Pacific coast mildness, abrupt North Atlantic shifts all correct.
sub.limitation: minor: T8 ignores Norway's Scandes; T1 'leaves the Gulf of Mexico' oversimplifies.

sub.name: Calibration and transparency
sub.example: T4 flags going beyond Alley; bases mark speakers' own extensions.
sub.limitation: minor: T3, T9 'biggest piece' claims carry confidence with no evidence offered.

sub.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
sub.example: T3 concedes Vancouver counterexample; T9 narrows claim explicitly.
sub.limitation: minor: T9 shifts from 'biggest piece' to 'least afford to lose', a reframing.

sub.name: Identification of the actual concern
sub.example: Section A names the ocean-versus-winds split as the decisive uncertainty.
sub.limitation: minor: whether user wants explanation or climate-risk view never asked.

sub.name: Meaningful use of personal context
sub.example: Uses user's Europe-Canada comparison, naming Labrador and Hudson Bay.
sub.limitation: material: which places the user compares never asked or used.

sub.name: Fit with goals and values
sub.example: Section E splits understanding today from forecasting circulation change.
sub.limitation: material: user's goal inferred, never confirmed or questioned.

sub.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
sub.example: T7 ties the split to Europe's exposure if Atlantic circulation weakens.
sub.limitation: material: stakes stay generic; no invented context but none tailored.

sub.name: Responsiveness to information
sub.example: Section E branches: explain today versus judge weakened circulation.
sub.limitation: material: no direct question to the user about purpose or locations.

sub.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
sub.example: Section D asks whether user sought one cause or combined causes.
sub.limitation: material: curiosity versus climate worry never offered as alternative motives.

sub.name: Examination of assumptions
sub.example: T2 exposes the latitude-plus-single-cause assumption via Pacific coast.
sub.limitation: minor: user's assumption that latitude should predict climate left implicit.

sub.name: Clarification of values and priorities
sub.example: Section E contrasts understanding the present with forecasting change.
sub.limitation: material: no priorities for the user named or weighed.

sub.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
sub.example: T7 hints Europe 'would feel it' under weaker circulation.
sub.limitation: material: possible climate anxiety or popular Gulf Stream myth never surfaced.

sub.name: Agency and reflective ownership
sub.example: T10 leaves fragility-versus-contribution open for the user to weigh.
sub.limitation: minor: Section D's single reflective question is thin.

sub.name: Definition of the decision and options
sub.example: Section E frames two uses: explanation now or forecasting change.
sub.limitation: material: no real choice defined; options loosely framed.

sub.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
sub.example: Section E notes combined picture beats any single cause.
sub.limitation: material: no cost of adopting either framing stated.

sub.name: Identification of decisive conditions
sub.example: Section E: Pacific coast mild without Gulf Stream favours combined picture.
sub.limitation: material: no threshold for ocean share that would change the forecast view.

sub.name: Treatment of uncertainty
sub.example: T7 isolates the ocean-atmosphere split as the consequential unknown.
sub.limitation: minor: well-known atmospheric dominance of heat transport never stated.

sub.name: Proportionate next steps
sub.example: Section E: compare published ocean and atmospheric heat-transport estimates.
sub.limitation: minor: step vague; no source type or starting point named.

sub.name: Accessible language
sub.example: T6 warehouse and delivery truck makes heat storage plain.
sub.limitation: minor: 'heat transport' in Section E unexplained for lay reader.

sub.name: Traceable arguments and references
sub.example: T5 'That's the gap' clearly points to T4's caveat.
sub.limitation: minor: T3 'its Pacific counterpart' vague about which places.

sub.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
sub.example: Ten turns, each roughly 45-60 words, evenly paced.
sub.limitation: minor: Sections D and E longer than any turn, dense.

sub.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
sub.example: Tracer, Reader, Comparer hold clearly different lenses; T9 shift explicit.
sub.limitation: minor: openers 'That's too neat', 'Fair', 'Good' sound alike across minds.

sub.name: Economy and sustained attention
sub.example: Turns mostly add a new point each.
sub.limitation: minor: Section D recaps causes already listed in T8-T9.

sub.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
sub.example: T7 links the credit split to Europe's fate if circulation weakens.
sub.limitation: material: stakes stay abstract until T7, mostly an academic dispute.

sub.name: Surprise and reversals
sub.example: T3 concedes, citing T2's Pacific counterexample; T9 narrows after T8.
sub.limitation: minor: reversals partial and expected; no genuine surprise.

sub.name: Personality and expressive voice
sub.example: T1 'opposite plumbing' gives the Tracer a confident voice.
sub.limitation: minor: Reader and Comparer voices fairly flat and neutral.

sub.name: Memorable delivery
sub.example: T6 'wind is the delivery truck and the ocean is the warehouse'.
sub.limitation: minor: few vivid concrete examples beyond Vancouver.

sub.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
sub.example: T7 'that sharpens the disagreement' raises momentum mid-debate.
sub.limitation: material: tone uniformly even; little rhythm or emotional variation.

strengths: Responsive chain: T5 names T4's gap, T6 answers, T7 turns it into a forecast question
Honest revision: T3 concedes the Pacific counterexample and T9 narrows the ocean claim
Sharp closing distinction in T10 between the most fragile and largest contributing cause
weaknesses: No question to the user about purpose or places compared; Sections D-E only infer goals
Magnitude claims (T3, T9) and the ocean-atmosphere split never given any evidence or estimate
Wind-pattern mechanism over eastern Canada missing; T8 ignores Norway's mountains
editorNotes: Require one turn to name and weigh at least one checkable magnitude or known estimate behind 'biggest piece' claims
Have the situation or a turn pose a direct question about the user's purpose with what each answer implies
Ask for two plausible motives (curiosity, climate concern) offered as alternatives in Section D
Require any new distinction introduced late to be used by a following turn, not only the last turn
